findings.title: Two optimizer comments describe a data flow the code does not have (warm-start alignment, buffer-series stash)
findings.claim: HeatPumpOptimizer._warm_start_starts' docstring calls the handed plan 'the same problem one step later', but after a 30-min re-plan (2 steps) coordinator._warm_seeded hands the previous schedule at offset 0; and OptimizationResult.buffer_temp_trajectory's comment says the model stashes the buffer series on itself for the terminal cost, but a valved solve (buffer_is_store) makes 0 sequence-valued writes on the ThermalModel.
findings.mechanism: _warm_seeded copies result.power_schedule verbatim (D0-s3's non-finding measured that aligning it changes no plan, so only the sentence is wrong); the last_buffer_trajectory stash was removed (D7-s2's non-finding: the terminal-cost closure takes buffer_temps as an argument) and the field comment at optimizer.py:1084-1089 still explains the field by it.

evidence.machine: B10-role leads seat, round-9 orchestrator cloud container (Linux 6.18, 4 cores), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: leads seat alone on the container except the orchestrator's idle session; counts are contention-immune

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:_warm_seeded (the array it attaches as _prev_shipped_plan) and heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model:ThermalModel.__setattr__ during HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize

perturbation.change: --shift (in memory, _warm_seeded drops the elapsed 2 steps) and --plant (a buffer series stashed on the model)

findings.metric_definition: (a) shift aligning the handed plan to the previous plan after one 30-min re-plan; (b) sequence-valued ThermalModel attribute writes during one valved solve.
findings.phenomenon_property: A comment that states how data reaches a symbol (aligned, stashed, copied) matches what the code delivers at that symbol.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n 'one step later\|stashes the series' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py; harness: tools/audit/round9/D5/leads/dataflow_comments.py

null_control.note: both counters move when the described flow is planted

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Reword optimizer.py:3100 (the handed plan is the previous plan on its own clock, a candidate the multi-start may reject) and optimizer.py:1087-1089 (drop the stash sentence).

findings.title: nightly_ha._async_check_a4 returns inside finally: an in-flight CancelledError or KeyboardInterrupt is swallowed
findings.claim: When the broken-price refresh raises a BaseException the inner handler does not catch (CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt) and the recovery refresh then raises, tests/nightly_ha.py:_async_check_a4 returns normally in 2 of 2 arms because of the `return` inside its finally (tests/nightly_ha.py:1274), and CPython 3.14 emits 1 SyntaxWarning compiling the file (PEP 765).
findings.mechanism: The recovery block in the outer finally catches Exception from the second async_refresh and returns; a return in finally discards any exception propagating from the try, so a cancellation or interrupt that reached the finally (a lane timeout, a runner stop) ends the A4 check as an ordinary recorded failure instead of stopping the run.

evidence.machine: B10-role leads seat, round-9 orchestrator cloud container (Linux 6.18, 4 cores), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: leads seat alone on the container except the orchestrator's idle session; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --fixed: the finally's return replaced by a flag checked after the block (same function, compiled in memory)

findings.metric_definition: Of 2 arms (CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt from the first refresh, recovery refresh raising), arms where _async_check_a4 returns instead of propagating; plus SyntaxWarnings on compile.
findings.phenomenon_property: No finally block in the suite or its lanes ends in return/break/continue, so an exception in flight always propagates (PEP 765).
findings.seam_rule: python3 -W error::SyntaxWarning -c "import py_compile,glob; [py_compile.compile(f, doraise=True) for f in glob.glob('tests/*.py')]" (each failure is a seam); harness: tools/audit/round9/D7/leads/nightly_finally_return.py

null_control.note: with the recovery refresh succeeding the in-flight exception propagates

findings.proposed_fix_scope: tests/nightly_ha.py:1266-1281: record the recovery failure in a flag and return after the finally.

findings.title: Two parsers of a rule's paths: frontmatter disagree on 2 of 6 legal shapes (rules_sync vs policy_lint)
findings.claim: On 2 of 6 probe frontmatters (a trailing YAML comment on a paths entry; a quoted list item under another key) rules_sync.mjs:parse and policy_lint.mjs:rulePaths return different path lists, so the generated .cursor/rules globs and the binding/budget checks read different scopes for one file; 0 of the 10 live rules diverge today.
findings.mechanism: rules_sync.mjs:parse takes every `- "..."` line anywhere in the frontmatter and requires `"\s*$` at line end; policy_lint.mjs:rulePaths reads only the `paths:` block and accepts trailing text. Neither calls the other, and rules_sync --check compares the .mdc with its own parse, so the divergence passes both checks.

evidence.unit: of 6 probe frontmatters with differing path lists (RESULT divergent_cells)
evidence.machine: leads box (shared 4-core Linux cloud container), CPython 3.14.0rc2 venv314 / node v22.22.2
evidence.contention_note: shared leads box, 3 other leads seats; a count, contention-immune

findings.instrumented_symbol: .claude/workflows/rules_sync.mjs:parse and .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs:rulePaths (both extracted from the files at run time)

perturbation.change: --perturb eol: rules_sync parse's `"([^"]+)"\s*$/gm` -> `"([^"]+)"/gm` (one-line edit, in memory)
perturbation.observed_value: divergent_cells 2 -> 1 (the trailing-comment cell agrees; the other-key cell remains)

findings.metric_definition: Probe rule frontmatters on which rules_sync parse().paths and policy_lint rulePaths() return different lists (JSON-compared).
findings.phenomenon_property: One rule file's paths: scope is parsed by one function, so the generated Cursor globs, rule-binding, role budgets and the always-loaded cap read the same list for every frontmatter.
findings.seam_rule: node tools/audit/round9/D11/leads/l3_frontmatter_parsers.mjs  (cells = frontmatter shapes; seams = every reader of a rule's paths: key: grep -n 'paths' .claude/workflows/*.mjs)

null_control.note: well-formed double-quoted block entries agree; capability, not incidence

findings.proposed_fix_scope: rules_sync.mjs reuses policy_lint's rulePaths (export it, or move it to a shared module) instead of its own regex; add the two probe shapes to rules_sync's --check fixtures.

findings.title: entities.py GOV pin reads governance.yml only: a new governance job in 3 of 3 other workflow files passes
findings.claim: The entities.py pin on governance_cost.py's GOV set stays green when a new job is added to pr-contract.yml, budget-raise-gate.yml or budget-raise-gate-rerun.yml (3 of 3), although GOV's own derivation rule names the first two as governance, and rerun-stale-verdict is already a governance job GOV does not name.
findings.mechanism: The pin checks GOV <= all job ids and _workflow_job_ids(governance.yml) <= GOV; the second arm reads only governance.yml, while governance_cost.py's comment derives GOV from governance.yml plus briefs, pr-contract.yml and budget-raise-gate.yml. Jobs in those files are never compared, so the set can go stale unseen (D13-s1 measured 64 s of rerun-stale-verdict missed).

evidence.machine: leads box (shared 4-core Linux cloud container), CPython 3.14.0rc2 venv314 / node v22.22.2

findings.title: Cold-water inlet default held three times: 3 of 5 sites ignore DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP when it moves
findings.claim: With const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP moved from 10.0 to 12.5, 3 of 5 production sites that resolve a cold-water default still deliver 10.0: bare ThermalParameters() (thermal_model.py:469 literal), sysid._sizing_model's plant (via that literal) and dhw_coil_draw_reduction's inlet_temp default (const.DHW_COLD_WATER_TEMP).
findings.mechanism: The default is spelled three ways: const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP (from_config and the options flow read it), a bare 10.0 on the ThermalParameters field, and const.DHW_COLD_WATER_TEMP, now only a default argument all three call sites override. They agree only because all three are 10.0 today.

evidence.unit: of 5 sites whose delivered default does not follow the moved constant (RESULT sites_not_following)
evidence.machine: leads box (shared 4-core Linux cloud container), CPython 3.14.0rc2 venv314 / node v22.22.2
evidence.contention_note: shared leads box, 3 other leads seats; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb literal: thermal_model.py:469 `dhw_inlet_temp: float = 10.0` -> `= const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP` (one-line edit, in memory)

findings.metric_definition: Of 5 production sites resolving a cold-water inlet default, those whose delivered value does not move when const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP is moved 10.0 -> 12.5.
findings.phenomenon_property: A configurable default is defined once and every site that falls back to it reads that one definition.

null_control.note: with the constant unmoved all sites agree at 10.0: no user-visible divergence today (hygiene)

findings.proposed_fix_scope: The ThermalParameters field defaults to const.DEFAULT_DHW_INLET_TEMP; DHW_COLD_WATER_TEMP is removed or aliased to it and dhw_coil_draw_reduction's inlet_temp made required (all 3 callers pass it).

findings.title: 4 of 5 ThermalModel per-step scratch members are written every step and read by no production consumer
findings.claim: Across four real solves (winter_single_dhw, dhw_cold_tank, wood_two_tank, wood_coil) production writes _step_dhw_refused, _step_dhw_floor_injected, _step_dhw_draw_kw and _step_wood_refused 31k-167k times each and no production function reads them (0 consumer reads, 0 loads outside thermal_model.py); only tests/features.py does (18 references).
findings.mechanism: The step functions book refused heat, floor injection and the debited draw on the model instance for a consumer that was never written: only _step_buffer_refused is read (simulate_trajectory). The _step_dhw_draw_kw comment says it lets 'energy accounting outside the model' balance the step; nothing outside reads it. D7-s3-01's reach census counts a store as reach, so it cannot see write-only members.

evidence.unit: of 5 _step_* members with production writes and 0 production consumer reads (RESULT write_only_members)
evidence.machine: leads box (shared 4-core Linux cloud container), CPython 3.14.0rc2 venv314 / node v22.22.2
evidence.contention_note: shared leads box, 3 other leads seats; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb reader: a one-line production read of self._step_dhw_draw_kw in ThermalModel.simulate_trajectory, compiled under thermal_model.py

findings.metric_definition: ThermalModel _step_* members with >=1 production write and 0 reads from production functions that never write that member, over four golden solves.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every member production writes is read by some production consumer; state computed only for tests is dead production work.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub /home/claude/venv314/bin/python tools/audit/round9/D7/leads/l3_write_only_scratch.py  (members = ThermalModel class attributes named _step_*; extend to any attribute with production stores and no production loads)

null_control.note: _step_buffer_refused, written by the same step functions, is read by simulate_trajectory: the instrument sees a live consumer

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Either give the ledgers their production consumer (the energy/refused-heat accounting their comments describe) or return them from the step for the tests that assert conservation instead of storing them on the instance; retarget the 18 features.py references.

findings.title: README's SEK currency fallback is unreachable under Home Assistant core, which defaults Config.currency to EUR
findings.claim: README.md says money is labelled 'SEK when the instance has none', but resolve_currency returns FALLBACK_CURRENCY for 0 of 2 Home Assistant core versions (2025.2.0, hacs.json's minimum, and 2026.2.3): core's Config.__init__ sets currency 'EUR', so an instance that never chose a currency is labelled EUR; only the test stub (FakeHass, currency 'SEK') produces SEK.
findings.mechanism: currency.resolve_currency falls back only on a falsy hass.config.currency; HA core initialises it to 'EUR' and validates a configured value, so the fallback and the README/docstring rationale describe the test double, not the counterpart.

evidence.unit: HA core versions (of 2) reaching the SEK fallback
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: reads HA core wheels fetched with pip download --no-deps into a mktemp root (or --wheels DIR)
